title: Former Eastlake boys basketball coach Matthew Taylor files EEOC charge, seeks reinstatement - NewsBreak
text:
By Sam Guzman No media credit provided. ,
57 minutes ago
EL PASO, Texas (KTSM) — Matthew Taylor, who was removed as Eastlake High School’s boys basketball head coach in December 2025, has filed a charge of discrimination with the Equal Employment Opportunity Commission (EEOC) and a grievance with Socorro Independent School District’s Eastlake High School, seeking immediate reinstatement as head coach.
The filing was confirmed by Jonathan Baeza of Baeza Law Firm, who represents Taylor.
Part of Baeza’s statement to KTSM on Wednesday, Dec. 21, reads:
“Mr. Taylor was recently removed from his coaching position. He has filed a charge of discrimination with the EEOC and intends to pursue his claims. He has also filed a grievance seeking immediate reinstatement as head basketball coach.”
Taylor has missed Eastlake’s last 11 games. He was removed from the position on December 15, just days after the team’s trip to Pflugerville, Texas for a tournament from Dec. 11-13, 2025.
When asked about the reason for Taylor’s removal on Dec. 22, SISD said it could not comment further, citing the matter as a personnel issue.
According to sources, Taylor missed just two of the team’s five games during the three-day tournament in Pflugerville.
Baeza’s statement also shed light on what led to Taylor’s removal:
“The allegations suggesting Mr. Taylor posed a safety risk and left students unattended are false. When Mr. Taylor experienced a medical episode related to a disability protected under the ADA, he handled it responsibly. At all times, students were properly supervised and no students were ever in danger or left alone. Rather than receiving support for addressing a medical issue, Mr. Taylor lost his coaching position.
The Americans with Disabilities Act protects employees with physical and mental health conditions—including PTSD and other mental health disabilities. Workers have the right to ask for reasonable accommodations without being punished for it.
We need to do better supporting people dealing with mental health challenges, especially our veterans and teachers who give so much to our communities. No one should lose their job for asking for help.
We’re confident the legal process will show the truth of what happened here.”
Taylor is a U.S. Army combat veteran who served four years on active duty.
SISD was contacted for comment on Wednesday but again said it could not comment on personnel matters.
Taylor remains employed at Eastlake High School as a teacher, according to SISD on Dec. 22.
Assistant coach Eric Martinez is currently serving as the team’s interim head coach.
Since Dec. 19, student-athletes on the Eastlake boys basketball team have staged protests before games, holding multiple signs expressing their belief that Taylor was wrongfully terminated.
This season, Eastlake has emerged as one of the top teams in the city, posting a 23-6 record.
The highlight of Eastlake’s season came when the Falcons defeated Chapin, snapping the Huskies’ 100-game winning streak against El Paso teams. Eastlake became the first El Paso team to beat Chapin since Andress did so on Jan. 30, 2021.
Right now, Eastlake is 5-0 in District 1-6A play and remains in contention for the district championship.
Taylor was promoted to Eastlake’s boys basketball head coach in September 2023, after previously serving as an assistant under former head coach Jim Moreno.
In his first season as head coach during the 2023-24 campaign, Taylor led the Falcons to a 21-15 record. Eastlake followed that with a 24-9 record during the 2024-25 season, which included a bi-district championship.
